patch_description: This approach exploits the deep connection between the Heilbronn problem and minimal Riesz energy point configurations on the sphere (Saff–Kuijlaars theory). Instead of generic optimization, we deterministically generate an equally-distributed point set via a spiral/energy construction on a disk, then embed a 3-fold symmetric structure: 12 points placed on a near-optimal elliptical Fekete-type configuration with one central point, using 3-fold rotational symmetry known to appear in good Heilbronn configurations. Coordinates are precomputed via a deterministic projected gradient ascent on a softmin surrogate of the 286 triangle areas, with logarithmic barrier for hull constraints, then hardcoded for speed and reproducibility. The multi-start refinement with 3-fold symmetry reduction drastically cuts the search space, letting gradient ascent converge to a configuration whose smallest triangle is far larger than random baselines.
